newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ to take EU to WTO to resolve butter dispute.
newsitem.headline: NZ to take EU to WTO to resolve butter dispute.

text.p: Agriculture Minister Lockwood Smith said on Tuesday New Zealand would be taking action against the European Union via the World Trade Organisation (WTO) to resolve a dispute over access of spreadable butter into European markets.
Smith made the comments after meeting Franz Fischler, EU Commissioner for Agriculture and Rural Development.
"Back in 1996 they announced a unilateral decision that our... utter, including spreadable butter, wouldn't quality for the country-specific tariff quota," Smith told reporters.
"We will be pursuing a resolution of the problem through the WTO."
Brussels has declared that spreadable butter was not true butter and has charged a higher entry tariff on shipments to Britain.
Smith said New Zealand had tried to reach a technical solution with the EU.

"That has not been possible and it seems now that first the New Zealand Dairy Board is likely to pursue court action to resolve the issue and the government will probably now be pursuing action through the World Trade Organisation -- what we
call a panel action -- to resolve the dispute."
He said it was not a hostile action but normal procedure under WTO rules.
Smith said it was disappointing that no resolution had been reached because New Zealand's relationship with the EU was good.
"This was an anomally. We don't normally do business this way. It is unfortunate but we must make sure the dairy industry doesn't suffer from this kind of thing."

Prime Minister Jim Bolger told reporters that New Zealand and the EU were in discussions to create an overall framework providing procedures and mechanisms for resolving issues that arise between the EU and New Zealand.
